text: Git branching is a powerful feature in version control that lets developers work on new ideas without disrupting the main codebase. When starting a new feature, you create a separate branch from the main branch, often called "main" or "master." This feature branch is your own workspace where you can experiment, make commits, and push changes freely. Once your work is complete, you create a pull request to propose merging your branch back into the main codebase. Reviewers can then comment on your changes, suggest fixes, or approve the merge. This workflow keeps the main branch stable, encourages collaboration, and makes it easy to track every change in the project’s history.
